scholarships.title: TU Graz High Potentials Scholarship Programme

existing.funding_period: over a period of up to two years
existing.description: The TU Graz High Potentials scholarship programme supports young talent from Austria and abroad with scholarships of up to EUR 8,800 for Bachelor's students and up to EUR 17,600 for Master's students over a period of up to two years. The programme is funded by partner companies, so individual scholarships carry their own sponsor requirements in addition to TU Graz's general criteria. TU Graz publishes separate application windows for the two degree levels: 15 October 2026 to 15 February 2027 for the Master's scholarships and 5 May 2027 to 7 July 2027 for the Bachelor's scholarships. Recipients also receive personal mentoring and access to a global alumni network, and TU Graz reports that it has supported around 200 students in total, with 13 scholarships awarded at the most recent ceremony in November 2025.
eligibility: Applying for a Bachelor's or Master's degree programme at TU Graz
Master's: proof of good academic achievements in the Bachelor's degree programme
Master's: admission to a Master's degree programme at TU Graz as of winter semester 2027/28 (for NAWI Graz Master's programmes the main enrolment must take place at TU Graz)
Master's: applicants do not need to have been admitted yet when applying for the scholarship
Applicants must meet the individual requirements of the specific partner scholarship they apply for
existing.eligibility_summary: Young talent from Austria and abroad who apply for a Bachelor's or Master's degree at TU Graz. For the Master's scholarships, TU Graz requires proof of good academic achievements in the Bachelor's programme and admission to a Master's degree programme at TU Graz as of winter semester 2027/28; applicants do not need to have been admitted when they apply. Individual partner scholarships may impose their own additional requirements.

existing.description: The One World Scholarship of the Afro-Asian Institute Salzburg is a partial scholarship of EUR 500 per month during the semester (October through June) for students from Africa, Asia, the Near and Middle East, Oceania, the Caribbean and Latin America who study in Salzburg. Applicants must already be enrolled in Austria or admitted to a regular degree programme, hold a student residence permit or visa, and be admitted to a regular Master's or PhD programme in Salzburg. Selection is a multi-stage process - online form until 12 July, verification of formal criteria, full application until 15 July, online interview, then acceptance or rejection - and the Institute states that applying does not guarantee a scholarship place because positions are very limited. Successful applicants are expected to show financial need, good study progress, interest in development-related issues and a willingness to attend monthly meetings and actively contribute to the programme. Regarding equally qualified individuals, priority is given to female students.
eligibility: Citizenship of a country in the Global South (Africa, Asia, Near and Middle East, Oceania, Caribbean or Latin America)
Already enrolled in Austria, or at least admitted to a regular degree programme
Admission to a regular Master's or PhD programme at a public university or university of applied sciences in Salzburg (University of Salzburg, UAS Salzburg, Mozarteum)
Residence permit 'student' or a student visa
Maximum age when applying: 30 for Master's studies (35 for mothers), 35 for doctoral studies (40 for mothers)
Demonstrated financial need and good academic performance
Commitment to attending monthly meetings and contributing to the programme
Interest in development-related issues reflected in the field of study, prior work experience or voluntary activities
Joint Master's programmes only possible by arrangement, with no guarantee
existing.eligibility_summary: Students from Africa, Asia, the Near and Middle East, Oceania, the Caribbean or Latin America who are already studying in Salzburg or at least admitted to a regular degree programme there, and who show interest in and commitment to sustainable development. Applicants must hold a student residence permit or student visa, must be admitted to a regular Master's or PhD programme at a public university or university of applied sciences in Salzburg, and must meet age limits of 30 (35 for mothers) for Master's and 35 (40 for mothers) for doctoral studies.
